def _day0_orders_for_strategy(strategy, money):
    """Compute the day-0 order list + money spent for a DAY0_STRATEGY.
    Affordability-gated exactly like the verified opening: each order is
    skipped (not fatal) if money runs out. Returns (orders, spent, leftover).
    Prices mirror _game_src.ANIMALS / CROPS / fib-hire exactly."""
    hires, items = DAY0_CANDIDATES.get(strategy, DAY0_CANDIDATES["VERIFIED"])
    orders = []
    start = money
    for i in range(hires):
        cost = _fib_cost(i)
        if money >= cost:
            orders.append(["HIRE"]); money -= cost
        else:
            break
    animal_cost = {"SHEEP": 500, "COW": 400, "GOOSE": 300}
    # TOMATO is not in main.py SEED_COST (the phase planner never buys it), but
    # the day-0 scanner prices it at its true cost 50 so TOMATO_SCALING is
    # reported honestly even though the planner can't use the seeds yet.
    seed_cost_full = dict(SEED_COST)
    seed_cost_full["TOMATO"] = 50
    for kind, item, qty in items:
        if kind == "ANIMAL":
            unit = animal_cost.get(item, 400)
            cost = unit * qty
            if money >= cost:
                orders.append(["BUY_ANIMAL", item, qty]); money -= cost
        elif kind == "SEED":
            unit = seed_cost_full.get(item, 10)
            cost = unit * qty
            if money >= cost:
                orders.append(["BUY_SEED", item, qty]); money -= cost
        elif kind == "PRODUCT":
            unit = BASE_PRICE.get(item, 25)   # ~price at I0 (inventory ~10000)
            cost = unit * qty
            if money >= cost:
                orders.append(["BUY_PRODUCT", item, qty]); money -= cost
    return orders, start - money, money


def _day0_scanner(money=3000):
    """Global initial scanner (reporting-only). Prices every DAY0_STRATEGY
    candidate and reports, per opening:
      - budget: spend / leftover after the exact order sequence
      - crew: hands hired day-0 (farmer + hands)
      - first income: earliest day the first sale lands (crop OR animal)
      - labor demand: estimated hands needed once the plan ramps
        (active crops to water + animals to feed/collect), using
        DAY0_FETCH_PER_ACTION actions per hand per day
      - gross season production proxy: crop units (seeds bought day-0) +
        animal units (max_held per interval over remaining days), unweighted
        by price so it is a *capacity* number, not a profit forecast.
    Prints a table (DEBUG_DAY_LOG / _DAY_LOG["day0"]) but never changes the
    opening itself — that is locked to DAY0_STRATEGY."""
    crop_first = {"WHEAT": 2, "CARROT": 2, "TOMATO": 8, "STRAWBERRY": 10, "MELON": 10}
    crop_max_yield = {"WHEAT": 6, "CARROT": 4, "TOMATO": 4, "STRAWBERRY": 4, "MELON": 6}
    animal_cost = {"SHEEP": 500, "COW": 400, "GOOSE": 300}
    animal_first = {"SHEEP": 6, "COW": 8, "GOOSE": 4}
    animal_interval = {"SHEEP": 3, "COW": 2, "GOOSE": 1}
    animal_max_held = {"SHEEP": 6, "COW": 6, "GOOSE": 4}

    out = {}
    for strat, (hires, items) in DAY0_CANDIDATES.items():
        orders, spent, leftover = _day0_orders_for_strategy(strat, money)
        animals = {}
        seeds = {}
        products = {}
        for kind, item, qty in items:
            if kind == "ANIMAL": animals[item] = animals.get(item, 0) + qty
            elif kind == "SEED": seeds[item] = seeds.get(item, 0) + qty
            elif kind == "PRODUCT": products[item] = products.get(item, 0) + qty

        # ---- structural blockers (can this opening actually run?) ----
        blocked = []
        if any(a == "GOOSE" for a in animals):
            blocked.append("NO_COOP_BUILD: geese can never be placed (no BUILD_COOP task gen)")
        if any(c == "TOMATO" for c in seeds):
            blocked.append("TOMATO_NOT_IN_PLANNER: seeds never planted (not in SEED_COST/phase plan)")
        if sum(animals.values()) > MAX_ANIMALS:
            blocked.append("ANIMALS>%d" % MAX_ANIMALS)
        # ---- cash runway warning (LEARNED 2026-08-09) ----
        # VERIFIED leaves 668 coins; WOOL_BARON/DAIRY_KING leave 68/88 and
        # BOTH crashed to 53k/63k vs 101k baseline. Days 1-11 the agent lives
        # on leftover + tiny wheat sales: with <~300 leftover it can only
        # re-hire hands and buy feed wheat — wave-2 melons, land, strawberries
        # and mid-game animals never happen. Capacity (gross_units) does NOT
        # predict reward; leftover working capital does.
        if leftover < 300 and animals:
            blocked.append("LOW_CASH_RUNWAY: %d leftover funds days 1-11 ops (VERIFIED keeps 668)" % leftover)

        # ---- first income day ----
        first_income = 99
        for item, qty in animals.items():
            first_income = min(first_income, animal_first[item])
        for item, qty in seeds.items():
            if item in crop_first:
                first_income = min(first_income, crop_first[item])

        # ---- labor demand proxy ----
        # Crops: each active crop needs ~1 WATER/day (watering capacity is the
        # binding constraint, ~40 actions/day max). Animals: feed/collect per
        # interval — each animal needs FEED every ~2 days + pickup on yield.
        crop_water_actions = sum(seeds.values())
        animal_actions = sum(qty for qty in animals.values())  # feed+care daily proxy
        labor_actions = crop_water_actions + animal_actions
        hands_needed = max(hires, 1 + int((labor_actions + DAY0_FETCH_PER_ACTION - 1)
                                          // DAY0_FETCH_PER_ACTION))

        # ---- gross season production proxy (capacity, unweighted) ----
        crop_units = sum(qty * crop_max_yield.get(item, 4)
                         for item, qty in seeds.items() if item in crop_max_yield)
        animal_units = 0
        for item, qty in animals.items():
            prod_days = max(0, 30 - animal_first[item]) // animal_interval[item]
            animal_units += qty * animal_max_held[item] * max(1, prod_days)

        out[strat] = {
            "orders": len(orders), "spend": spent, "leftover": leftover,
            "hires": len([o for o in orders if o[0] == "HIRE"]),
            "animals": dict(animals), "seeds": dict(seeds),
            "first_income_day": first_income,
            "hands_needed": hands_needed,
            "crop_units": crop_units, "animal_units": animal_units,
            "gross_units": crop_units + animal_units,
            "blocked": blocked,
        }
    return out


def _day0_animal_strategy(market_inv, market_prices, day=0, hour=0,
                          unlocked_shops=None):
    """Forecast-driven day-0 animal decision. Projects MILK and WOOL prices at
    the sheep first-yield day (earliest animal income) using the deterministic
    town-drain projection. When BOTH are projected below
    DAY0_ANIMAL_WEAK_RATIO (i.e. the herd won't pay back), returns a LIGHTER
    opening that shrinks animals (cash stays in melons/wheat). Otherwise
    returns the verified full opening. Reporting-only when the knob is OFF.
    The decision uses the SAME numbers the sell side sees (projected price
    ratios), so the agent decides the "max animals" constraint from the
    forecast instead of hard-coding it."""
    if not DYNAMIC_DAY0_ANIMALS:
        return DAY0_STRATEGY, {}
    try:
        steps = DAY0_ANIMAL_FIRST_YIELD * 24
        proj = _project_prices(market_inv, day, hour, steps,
                               unlocked_shops or [])
        milk_r = _price_ratio("MILK", proj)
        wool_r = _price_ratio("WOOL", proj)
        weak = (milk_r < DAY0_ANIMAL_WEAK_RATIO
                and wool_r < DAY0_ANIMAL_WEAK_RATIO)
        if weak:
            # Lighter herd: keep melons/wheat, drop animals to a minimum.
            # Only shrink — never grow past the verified composition.
            return "CROP_FIRST", {
                "milk_proj": round(milk_r, 2), "wool_proj": round(wool_r, 2),
                "weak": True, "why": "milk/wool premium projected weak at d%d" % (
                    DAY0_ANIMAL_FIRST_YIELD),
            }
        return DAY0_STRATEGY, {
            "milk_proj": round(milk_r, 2), "wool_proj": round(wool_r, 2),
            "weak": False, "why": "premium projected alive",
        }
    except Exception:
        return DAY0_STRATEGY, {}


def _day0_opening(money, strategy=None, market_inv=None, market_prices=None,
                  unlocked_shops=None):
    """Verified Day-0 opening script (budget 3000). Executes the strategy
    selected by DAY0_STRATEGY (default VERIFIED = the proven 116k baseline),
    or the forecast-driven animal decision when DYNAMIC_DAY0_ANIMALS is ON.
    Each order is affordability-gated so a cheaper start never overspends.
    Run _day0_scanner(money) first to see the full candidate table."""
    strat = strategy or DAY0_STRATEGY
    decision = {}
    if DYNAMIC_DAY0_ANIMALS:
        strat, decision = _day0_animal_strategy(
            market_inv, market_prices, 0, 0, unlocked_shops)
    orders, spent, leftover = _day0_orders_for_strategy(strat, money)
    return orders, leftover, strat, decision


def _record_day_log(day, money, forecast_free, market_prices, market_inv,
                    buy_orders, trend=None, expenses=None, opponent=None,
                    animal_phase=None, next_actions=None, outcome=None,
                    demand=None, recovery=None, opp_buys=None,
                    tile_map=None, late_game=None, goose=None):
    """One-line-per-day tracker: money, price ratios, tomorrow's price trend,
    projected expenses, buys, last buy days, and a compact REASON string that
    shows the agent's decision chain (why this route, why these buys/sells) so
    the QA harness / stdout exposes the thought patterns. Stored in _DAY_LOG;
    printed / appended when DEBUG_DAY_LOG is on. `animal_phase` is the
    price-gated animal-phase snapshot (see _animal_phase_report);
    `next_actions` is the next-day workload forecast (_forecast_next_day_actions)
    and `outcome` is the season-end projection (_project_outcome).
    `demand`/`recovery`/`opp_buys` are the market-awareness features
    (_market_demand_rate / _price_recovery_time / _infer_opponent_activity)."""
    global _DAY_LOG
    if _DAY_LOG is not None and _DAY_LOG.get("day") == day:
        return

    # ---- Compact reasoning summary (thought patterns for QA) ----
    reason_parts = []
    if isinstance(opponent, dict):
        ctr = opponent.get("counter")
        if isinstance(ctr, dict) and ctr.get("route"):
            reason_parts.append("route=%s@%.2fx" % (ctr["route"], ctr.get("route_ratio", 0)))
            if ctr.get("dump_before"):
                reason_parts.append("dump_before=%s" % ",".join(ctr["dump_before"]))
            if ctr.get("avoid"):
                reason_parts.append("avoid=%s" % ",".join(ctr["avoid"]))
        dt = opponent.get("dump_timing")
        if isinstance(dt, dict) and dt:
            crash = [p for p, r in dt.items()
                     if _float(r.get("price_after_dump", 1.0), 1.0)
                        < _float(r.get("best_before_dump", 1.0), 1.0)]
            if crash:
                reason_parts.append("crash_soon=%s" % ",".join(crash))
    buys = ["%s:%s" % (o[0], o[1] if len(o) > 1 else "") for o in buy_orders]
    if buys:
        reason_parts.append("buy=%s" % ",".join(buys))
    reason = " | ".join(reason_parts) if reason_parts else ""

    _DAY_LOG = {
        "day": day,
        "money": money,
        "forecast": dict(forecast_free) if forecast_free else {},
        "prices": _price_info(market_prices, market_inv),
        "trend": trend or {},
        "expenses": expenses or {},
        "buys": buys,
        "reason": reason,
        "last_buy_day": {
            "COW": _last_profitable_buy_day("COW", market_prices),
            "SHEEP": _last_profitable_buy_day("SHEEP", market_prices),
            "LAND": (30 - 12) if day < 30 else 0,   # _plan_land window
        },
        "day0": _day0_scanner(3000) if day == 0 else _DAY_LOG.get("day0"),
        "day0_strategy": DAY0_STRATEGY if day == 0 else _DAY_LOG.get("day0_strategy"),
        "opponent": opponent or {},
        "animal_phase": animal_phase or {},
        "next_actions": next_actions or {},
        "outcome": outcome or {},
        "demand": demand or {},
        "recovery": recovery or {},
        "opp_buys": opp_buys or {},
        "tile_map": tile_map or {},
        "late_game": late_game or {},
        "goose": goose or {},
    }
    if DEBUG_DAY_LOG:
        opp_line = _DAY_LOG["opponent"]
        pr_line = _DAY_LOG["prices"]
        ap_line = _DAY_LOG["animal_phase"]
        na_line = _DAY_LOG["next_actions"]
        oc_line = _DAY_LOG["outcome"]
        dm_line = _DAY_LOG["demand"]
        rc_line = _DAY_LOG["recovery"]
        ob_line = _DAY_LOG["opp_buys"]
        tm_line = _DAY_LOG["tile_map"]
        lg_line = _DAY_LOG["late_game"]
        line = ("[DAY %02d] money=%6d prices=%s reason=%s opp=%s" % (
            day, money, pr_line, reason if reason else "-",
            opp_line if opp_line else "-"))
        if tm_line:
            line += (" | tiles={unlocked:%d empty:%d avg_dist:%s max_dist:%d far:%d}" % (
                tm_line.get("unlocked", 0), tm_line.get("empty", 0),
                tm_line.get("avg_dist", 0), tm_line.get("max_dist", 0),
                len(tm_line.get("far_tiles", []))))
        if lg_line:
            line += (" | late={empty:%d util:%.2f free:%d plantable:%s}" % (
                lg_line.get("empty_now", 0), lg_line.get("utilization", 0),
                lg_line.get("will_free", 0), lg_line.get("plantable_late", {})))
        if dm_line:
            line += (" | demand=%s" % (dm_line,))
        if rc_line:
            line += (" | recovery=%s" % (rc_line,))
        if ob_line:
            line += (" | opp_buys=%s" % (ob_line,))
        if ap_line:
            line += (" | animal_phase=active:%s placed:%d milk:%.2f->%.2f "
                     "wool:%.2f->%.2f own:%s" % (
                         ap_line.get("active"), ap_line.get("placed", 0),
                         ap_line.get("milk_now", 0), ap_line.get("milk_self", 0),
                         ap_line.get("wool_now", 0), ap_line.get("wool_self", 0),
                         ap_line.get("own_units", {})))
        if na_line:
            line += (" | next_actions={%s} total=%d" % (
                ",".join("%s:%d" % (k, v) for k, v in na_line.items()
                         if k != "total"),
                na_line.get("total", 0)))
        if oc_line:
            line += (" | outcome=proj:%d today:%d rate:%d days:%d note:%s" % (
                oc_line.get("projected_final", 0), oc_line.get("today", 0),
                oc_line.get("daily_rate", 0), oc_line.get("days_left", 0),
                oc_line.get("note", "")))
        print(line)
        if day == 0 and _DAY_LOG.get("day0"):
            try:
                with open("day_log.txt", "a") as _f:
                    _f.write("[DAY 00] day0_strategy=%s day0=%s\n" % (
                        _DAY_LOG.get("day0_strategy"),
                        {k: {kk: vv for kk, vv in v.items() if kk != "orders"}
                         for k, v in _DAY_LOG["day0"].items()}))
            except Exception:
                pass
        try:
            with open("day_log.txt", "a") as _f:
                _f.write(line + "\n")
        except Exception:
            pass


def _build_sell_orders(day, hour, shed, global_inv, placed_animals,
                       market_inv, market_prices, sell_slots, endgame,
                       daily_sold, shed_pressure, counter_timing=None,
                       counter_log=None, recovery=None, demand=None):
    """Timing-aware sell order builder. Price-aware: premium items are sold
    one unit at a time while the MARGINAL price stays >= SELL_MIN_RATIO*base,
    and the daily budget doubles when the market pays >= SELL_HIGH_RATIO*base.
    `daily_sold` is mutated in place (per-day sold counters).

    Opponent counter (OPPONENT_CROP_COUNTER, OFF default): `counter_timing` is
    the `_opponent_dump_timing` report. When the opponent's next wave will
    LOWER a premium item's price below the best window we can catch today
    (price_after_dump < best_before_dump), we ACCELERATE selling that item
    NOW — before their supply hits the shared market. The marginal floor still
    guards every unit, so we never oversell into our own crash. `counter_log`
    (optional mutable dict) records which items the counter actually boosted,
    for the day tracker / reasoning trace.

    Recovery/demand awareness (RECOVERY_AWARE_SELL, ON): `recovery` =
    {item: steps-to-recover} and `demand` = {item: units/turn} from the market
    scanners. Short recovery / high demand -> HOLD (the climb continues);
    long recovery / low demand -> ACCELERATE (the premium is fleeting). This
    is the shops-demand-driven milk/wool sell timing from the briefing."""
    turn_index = day * 24 + hour
    near_tick = (turn_index % 12) in (10, 11)

    sell_candidates = []
    for item in SELLABLE_ITEMS:
        qty = _sellable_inventory(item, shed, global_inv, day, placed_animals)
        if qty <= 0: continue
        mkt_inv = _int(_safe_get(market_inv, item, 10000), 10000)
        safe = SELL_SAFE_INVENTORY.get(item, 10100)
        sell_qty = 0

        # ---- EARLY-DUMP TIMING (user strategy, early cash trough) ----
        # Days 1..EARLY_DUMP_END_DAY are the cash trough (money ~44-305). If
        # the opponent's first harvest/dump of THIS item is imminent AND will
        # crash the price (price_after_dump < price_now), sell our stock NOW
        # into the pre-dump price — the early cash arrives before the market
        # collapses. Marginal floor still guards every unit.
        if (EARLY_DUMP_TIMING and 1 <= day <= EARLY_DUMP_END_DAY
                and counter_timing and item in counter_timing):
            dt = counter_timing[item]
            after = _float(dt.get("price_after_dump", 1.0), 1.0)
            now = _float(dt.get("price_now", 1.0), 1.0)
            next_dump = _int(dt.get("next_dump_day", 99), 99)
            units = _int(dt.get("units", 0), 0)
            if (next_dump - day) <= EARLY_DUMP_LEAD_DAYS \
                    and units >= EARLY_DUMP_MIN_UNITS \
                    and after < now:
                # Sell as much as the marginal floor allows (never below floor).
                early_max_q = 0
                for _ in range(min(qty, 12)):
                    if _market_price(item, mkt_inv + early_max_q) < \
                            SELL_MIN_RATIO * BASE_PRICE.get(item, 1):
                        break
                    early_max_q += 1
                if early_max_q > sell_qty:
                    sell_qty = early_max_q
                    if counter_log is not None:
                        counter_log[item] = "early dump d%d (now %.2f, after %.2f)" % (
                            next_dump, now, after)

        if item in PREMIUM_DAILY_BUDGET:
            if endgame: sell_qty = qty
            elif (EARLY_LIVESTOCK_SELL and item in ("MILK", "WOOL")
                    and 1 <= day <= EARLY_LIVESTOCK_SELL_DAYS):
                # Strategy #3 early-aggression window: sell ALL fetched milk/
                # wool as soon as it reaches the shed to fund faster scaling.
                # Only the marginal floor caps it (never sell below floor).
                sell_qty = qty
            elif PRICE_AWARE_SELL:
                # True price control: market orders execute one unit at a
                # time and re-quote the price after each unit, so we only
                # sell units whose MARGINAL price stays at/above the
                # reservation floor (SELL_MIN_RATIO * base). In a glut we
                # hold and let the town drain the market back up; at a
                # scarcity premium we sell up to the (scaled) budget.
                base = BASE_PRICE.get(item, 1)
                min_price = SELL_MIN_RATIO * base
                budget = PREMIUM_DAILY_BUDGET[item]
                if _price_ratio(item, market_prices) >= SELL_HIGH_RATIO:
                    budget = budget * SELL_HIGH_BUDGET_MULT
                # RECOVERY/DEMAND AWARE (briefing Pillar 1/3/4): the town
                # drain either rescues a premium (fast recovery -> hold) or
                # abandons it (slow recovery -> our own supply crashes it,
                # sell more now). Demand rate tells us whether the climb is
                # shop-driven (real, hold) or center-only (fleeting, sell).
                if RECOVERY_AWARE_SELL:
                    # Only MILK/WOOL/STRAWBERRY are steady streams where
                    # "sell before the fleeting premium dies" makes sense.
                    # MELON is a BULK one-time wave: dumping it all at once
                    # (budget x2 + shed-pressure) crashes the price and
                    # forfeits the slow recovery (measured: day-19 MELON 57
                    # dump -> 0.85x; spread sales recover). Never accelerate
                    # melon dumps.
                    if item != "MELON":
                        rt = _int(_safe_get(recovery, item, -1), -1)
                        dr = _float(_safe_get(demand, item, 0.0), 0.0)
                        if rt >= 0:
                            if rt <= RECOVERY_HOLD_STEPS:
                                # Fast drain: the price recovers soon, the climb
                                # continues -> keep the normal budget (hold).
                                pass
                            elif rt >= RECOVERY_DUMP_STEPS and dr < RECOVERY_DEMAND_HOLD:
                                # Slow recovery + weak demand: this premium is
                                # fleeting. Accelerate before our own supply (and
                                # any opponent dump) pushes it to the floor.
                                budget = budget * RECOVERY_DUMP_MULT
                        elif dr < RECOVERY_DEMAND_HOLD:
                            # Already scarce but shop demand is weak: the scarcity
                            # is center-only and will fade; don't overshoot.
                            budget = budget  # normal
                rem = budget - daily_sold[item]
                if rem > 0:
                    inv = mkt_inv
                    max_q = 0
                    cap = min(rem, qty)
                    for _ in range(cap):
                        if _market_price(item, inv + max_q) < min_price:
                            break
                        max_q += 1
                    if shed_pressure >= 0.9:
                        max_q = max(max_q, min(qty, max(1, budget // 2)))
                    sell_qty = max_q
                    # OPPONENT COUNTER (Phase 2): their next wave will crash
                    # this item -> sell everything profitable BEFORE it lands.
                    # Only fire when the dump is IMMINENT (within the lead
                    # window): if it is still days out, the best_before_dump
                    # window (projected) is HIGHER than today, so dumping now
                    # forfeits the climb (measured: day-11 dump-before at 1.07
                    # lost the day-14 window at 1.11). `best_day` is where the
                    # price peaks before their wave — we wait until we are
                    # inside the lead window so we sell at/near that peak.
                    if (OPPONENT_CROP_COUNTER and counter_timing
                            and item in counter_timing):
                        dt = counter_timing[item]
                        after = _float(dt.get("price_after_dump", 1.0), 1.0)
                        best = _float(dt.get("best_before_dump", 1.0), 1.0)
                        now = _float(dt.get("price_now", 1.0), 1.0)
                        next_dump = _int(dt.get("next_dump_day", 99), 99)
                        imminent = (next_dump - day) <= CROP_COUNTER_DUMP_LEAD_DAYS
                        if imminent and after < best and after < now:
                            counter_max_q = 0
                            counter_cap = qty
                            for _ in range(counter_cap):
                                if _market_price(item, inv + counter_max_q) < min_price:
                                    break
                                counter_max_q += 1
                            if counter_max_q > sell_qty:
                                sell_qty = counter_max_q
                                if counter_log is not None:
                                    counter_log[item] = "boost near dump d%d (now %.2f, after %.2f)" % (next_dump, now, after)
            else:
                rem = PREMIUM_DAILY_BUDGET[item] - daily_sold[item]
                if rem > 0 and mkt_inv < safe: sell_qty = min(qty, rem)
            daily_sold[item] += sell_qty
        elif item == "EGG" and _geese_on():
            # Goose Pillar 5: town center drains eggs x1/x2/x4 at days 0/10/20.
            # Before day 20 demand is weak (and eggs are glut-resilient, so
            # they hold value) -> HOLD eggs in the shed. After day 20 the town
            # center quadruples consumption, draining the market and raising
            # price -> liquidate stored eggs then. Bakery/Brunch add shop
            # drain on top (scanner reports the demand rate).
            if endgame:
                sell_qty = qty
            elif day >= 20:
                sell_qty = min(qty, 12)   # peak demand window, sell stored stock
            else:
                sell_qty = min(qty, 2)    # hold early; only trim shed pressure
        elif item == "FERTILIZER":
            if endgame: sell_qty = qty
            elif near_tick:
                sell_qty = min(qty, 6) if mkt_inv < safe else min(2, qty)
            else:
                if mkt_inv < safe: sell_qty = min(3, qty)
        elif item == "WHEAT":
            if endgame: sell_qty = qty
            elif near_tick:
                sell_qty = min(qty, 10) if mkt_inv < 10000 else min(4, qty)
            else:
                if mkt_inv < 10000: sell_qty = min(6, qty)
        elif endgame: sell_qty = qty
        else:
            if mkt_inv < safe:
                room = safe - mkt_inv
                max_tr = 2 if item in PREMIUM_ITEMS else 6
                sell_qty = min(qty, max(1, room), max_tr)
            else:
                sell_qty = min(2, qty) if item in PREMIUM_ITEMS else min(3, qty)
            if near_tick:
                sell_qty = max(sell_qty, min(qty, 4))
            if shed_pressure >= 0.85:
                sell_qty = max(sell_qty, min(qty, 2))

        sell_qty = min(sell_qty, qty)
        if sell_qty > 0:
            sell_candidates.append((item, sell_qty, BASE_PRICE.get(item, 1) * sell_qty))

    sell_candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[2], reverse=True)
    return [["SELL", item, qty] for item, qty, _ in sell_candidates[:sell_slots]]

# MAIN AGENT
# ==========================================================================

def agent(obs):
    global _DAILY_SOLD, _TASK_CLAIMS, _DAY_LOG, _GEESE_ACTIVE

    if obs.get("step", 0) == 0:
        _reset_state()

    try:
        if not isinstance(obs, dict):
            return _pass()

        player = _int(obs.get("player", 0), 0)
        day = _int(obs.get("day", 0), 0)
        hour = _int(obs.get("hour", 0), 0)

        farms = obs.get("farms", [])
        private = obs.get("private", {})
        if not farms or player >= len(farms):
            return _pass()

        me = farms[player]
        if not isinstance(me, dict):
            return _pass()

        money = _float(me.get("money", 0.0), 0.0)
        tiles = me.get("tiles", [])
        farmer = me.get("farmer", [0, 0])
        hands = me.get("hands", [])
        unlocked_quads = me.get("unlocked_quadrants", ["NW"])
        hires_today = _int(me.get("hires_today", 0), 0)

        unlocked_cnt = max(1, len(unlocked_quads))
        unlocked_set = set(unlocked_quads)

        # Goose enable decision (once): geese activate ONLY if the static
        # ENABLE_GEESE knob is on AND (if GEESE_DEMAND_ENABLE) an egg shop
        # unlocked early. Default: both off (A/B showed geese regress even
        # with Bakery+Brunch, so this stays OFF unless the user flips both).
        if not _GEESE_ACTIVE and ENABLE_GEESE:
            if not GEESE_DEMAND_ENABLE:
                _GEESE_ACTIVE = True
            else:
                shops = _safe_get(_safe_get(obs, "town", {}), "unlocked_shops", [])
                if day <= 8 and ("BAKERY" in shops or "BRUNCH_SPOT" in shops):
                    _GEESE_ACTIVE = True

        if not _is_sequence(tiles) or len(farmer) < 2:
            return _pass()
        if not _is_sequence(hands):
            hands = []

        farmer_pos = (farmer[0], farmer[1])
        if not _in_bounds(tiles, farmer_pos[0], farmer_pos[1]):
            return _pass()

        unit_positions = [farmer_pos]
        for h in hands:
            if _is_sequence(h) and len(h) >= 2:
                unit_positions.append((h[0], h[1]))
            else:
                unit_positions.append((0, 0))

        shed = _safe_get(private, "shed", {})
        seeds = _safe_get(private, "seeds", {})
        inventories = _safe_get(private, "inventories", [])
        if not isinstance(inventories, list):
            inventories = []

        market_info = _safe_get(obs, "market", {})
        market_inv = _safe_get(market_info, "inventory", {})
        market_prices = market_info.get("prices", {})

        global_inv = {}
        for k, v in shed.items(): global_inv[k] = global_inv.get(k, 0) + _int(v, 0)
        for inv in inventories:
            if isinstance(inv, dict):
                for k, v in inv.items(): global_inv[k] = global_inv.get(k, 0) + _int(v, 0)

        active_crops = _scan_active_crops(tiles)
        days_left = max(0, 30 - day)
        placed_animals = _count_placed_animals(tiles)
        forecast_free = (_forecast_free_tiles(tiles, day)
                         if (ENABLE_HARVEST_FORECAST or FORECAST_DRIVES_HANDS)
                         else {})

        planning_workers = max(len(unit_positions),
                               _desired_hands(day, money, active_crops,
                                              placed_animals, forecast_free,
                                              unlocked_cnt) + 1)
        expected_workers = planning_workers

        target_crops = _choose_target_crops(day, hour, money, seeds, active_crops,
                                            market_inv, planning_workers, unlocked_cnt)
        plant_budget = _plant_budget(target_crops, seeds, active_crops, planning_workers, unlocked_cnt)
        if hour >= 22:
            for c in list(plant_budget.keys()): plant_budget[c] = 0

        tasks = _generate_tasks(tiles, day, target_crops, plant_budget, MAX_NEW_PLANTS_PER_TURN,
                                shed, inventories, unlocked_set, expected_workers,
                                market_prices)

        unit_actions, unit_types, unit_prios = _assign_tasks_zoned(
            tasks, unit_positions, tiles, unlocked_set, plant_budget, inventories, day)

        # Weed override
        for i, upos in enumerate(unit_positions):
            x, y = upos
            if _in_bounds(tiles, x, y) and _is_weed(tiles[y][x]):
                if not PRIORITY_AWARE_WEED_OVERRIDE:
                    unit_actions[i] = ["DIG"]
                elif unit_prios[i] < WEED_OVERRIDE_CRITICAL_THRESHOLD:
                    unit_actions[i] = ["DIG"]

        # ==================== MARKET ORDERS ====================
        # Budget is planned as a whole by _plan_market: land -> feed -> hires
        # -> animals -> seeds, each turn-aware. Only the verified Day-0 opening
        # is a fixed script (budget 3000 -> ~25 coin leftover).
        buy_orders = []
        money_est = money

        # Opponent lane map (public farm, see _scan_opponent_farm). Only
        # computed when the analysis knob is ON; guarded so a scan failure
        # degrades to {} and never affects the turn (the outer try would
        # otherwise turn a scan error into a whole-turn PASS).
        opponent = {}
        if ENABLE_OPPONENT_ANALYSIS:
            try:
                opp_farm = None
                for i, f in enumerate(farms):
                    if i != player:
                        opp_farm = f
                        break
                opp_scan = _scan_opponent_farm(opp_farm)
                opponent = _opponent_lane_analysis(opp_scan, day)
                # Timing-race counter decision (frozen once, see helpers).
                # Reporting-only; actions gate behind OPPONENT_CROP_COUNTER.
                unlocked_shops = _safe_get(_safe_get(obs, "town", {}),
                                           "unlocked_shops", [])
                counter = _get_counter_decision(
                    opp_scan, tiles, day, market_inv, unlocked_shops)
                if counter:
                    opponent["counter"] = counter
                # SELL-side counter timing (Phase 1 reporting-only):
                # trajectory AFTER their next dump + best window before it.
                opponent["dump_timing"] = _opponent_dump_timing(
                    opp_scan, market_inv, day, hour, unlocked_shops)
            except Exception as _oe:
                if DEBUG_DAY_LOG:
                    print("OPP_SCAN_ERR: %r" % (_oe,))
                opponent = {}

        if day == 0 and hour == 0:
            buy_orders, money_est, _d0_strat, _d0_decision = _day0_opening(
                money, None, market_inv, market_prices, unlocked_shops)
        else:
            unlocked_shops = _safe_get(_safe_get(obs, "town", {}), "unlocked_shops", [])
            buy_orders, money_est = _plan_market(
                day, hour, money, tiles, seeds, active_crops, placed_animals,
                unlocked_cnt, unlocked_set, market_prices, global_inv, hires_today,
                planning_workers, shed_pressure, forecast_free,
                market_inv, unlocked_shops, opponent)

        sell_slots = max(0, 10 - len(buy_orders))
        endgame = day >= LIQUIDATION_DAY or shed_pressure >= SHED_PRESSURE_LIMIT

        # Market-awareness features (recovery + demand) are used BOTH by the
        # sell builder (RECOVERY_AWARE_SELL) and the day tracker. Compute once
        # here, before selling, so the sell decisions see the same numbers.
        demand = None
        recovery = None
        if ENABLE_EARLY_SCANNERS:
            demand = _market_demand_rate(unlocked_shops, day)
            recovery = {}
            for it in BASE_PRICE:
                rt = _price_recovery_time(it, market_inv, day, hour,
                                          unlocked_shops)
                if rt >= 0:
                    recovery[it] = rt

        # ---- Day tracker (once per day, at the morning plan) ----
        unlocked_shops = _safe_get(_safe_get(obs, "town", {}), "unlocked_shops", [])
        trend = _price_trend(market_inv, market_prices, day, hour, unlocked_shops)
        expenses = _project_expenses(
            day, money, active_crops, placed_animals, seeds, global_inv,
            market_prices, unlocked_cnt, hires_today)
        # Early-game prediction scanners (reporting-only; see knobs).
        next_actions = None
        outcome = None
        opp_buys = None
        tile_map = None
        late_game = None
        goose = None
        if ENABLE_EARLY_SCANNERS:
            next_actions = _forecast_next_day_actions(
                tiles, day, placed_animals, active_crops, seeds)
            outcome = _project_outcome(
                day, money, active_crops, placed_animals, global_inv,
                market_prices, unlocked_cnt, seeds)
            tile_map = _tile_distance_map(tiles, unlocked_set)
            late_game = _late_game_utilization(tiles, day, seeds, active_crops,
                                               unlocked_cnt)
            if _geese_on():
                goose = _goose_profitability(
                    market_inv, market_prices, day, hour, unlocked_shops,
                    placed_animals)
            # Opponent buy inference: compare market inventory vs the
            # previous turn's snapshot (deterministic town drain).
            global _PREV_MARKET_INV
            opp_buys = _infer_opponent_activity(_PREV_MARKET_INV, market_inv,
                                                unlocked_shops, day)
            _PREV_MARKET_INV = dict(market_inv) if isinstance(market_inv, dict) else None
        _record_day_log(day, money, forecast_free, market_prices, market_inv,
                        buy_orders, trend, expenses, opponent,
                        _animal_phase_report(market_inv, market_prices, day,
                                             hour, unlocked_shops,
                                             placed_animals)
                        if ANIMAL_PHASE_CONTROL and isinstance(market_inv, dict)
                        else None,
                        next_actions, outcome, demand, recovery, opp_buys,
                        tile_map, late_game, goose)

        daily_sold = _DAILY_SOLD
        if daily_sold["day"] != day:
            daily_sold.update({"day": day, "MELON": 0, "STRAWBERRY": 0, "MILK": 0, "WOOL": 0})

        # ---- Selling logic (timing‑aware) ----
        counter_log = {}
        sell_orders = _build_sell_orders(
            day, hour, shed, global_inv, placed_animals, market_inv,
            market_prices, sell_slots, endgame, daily_sold, shed_pressure,
            opponent.get("dump_timing") if isinstance(opponent, dict) else None,
            counter_log, recovery, demand)

        # ---- Reasoning trace (thought patterns for QA) ----
        # The day log shows WHAT the scanner sees (opp=) and WHY sells/buys
        # were chosen. counter_log records the items the opponent-counter
        # actually boosted; _record_day_log stores it so the harness/stdout
        # shows the decision chain.
        if counter_log:
            _DAY_LOG["counter_actions"] = counter_log
            if DEBUG_DAY_LOG:
                ca_line = "[DAY %02d] counter_actions=%s" % (day, counter_log)
                print(ca_line)
                try:
                    with open("day_log.txt", "a") as _f:
                        _f.write(ca_line + "\n")
                except Exception:
                    pass

        market = sell_orders + buy_orders
        final_market = []
        for order in market:
            if not _is_sequence(order) or len(order) == 0: continue
            if order[0] == "SELL" and len(order) >= 3:
                item, qty = order[1], _int(order[2], 0)
                if _sellable_inventory(item, shed, global_inv, day, placed_animals) >= qty:
                    final_market.append(order)
            else:
                final_market.append(order)
        market = final_market[:10]

        farmer_action = unit_actions[0] if unit_actions else ["PASS"]
        hand_actions = unit_actions[1:] if len(unit_actions) > 1 else []

        return {"farmer": farmer_action, "hands": hand_actions, "market": market}

    except Exception:
        return _pass()

# CV Builder (Web Edition)

A **pure HTML/JS** version of the offline CV builder. Drag & drop your existing CV, let the app parse it with a local LLM (or built-in fallback parser), edit every field in a clean form, and download a professional DOCX — all in your browser. **Nothing is uploaded or stored.**

## Features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| **Multiple formats** | Parse PDF, DOCX, TXT, and images (PNG/JPG via OCR) |
| **LLM integration** | Send extracted text to any OpenAI-compatible local LLM (Ollama, LM Studio, etc.) |
| **Fallback parser** | Built-in regex-based parser works even without an LLM |
| **Full editing** | Every extracted field is editable before generation |
| **DOCX export** | Generates a clean, professional Word document |
| **Dark / light mode** | Toggle with your system or manual switch |
| **Keyboard shortcuts** | <kbd>Ctrl+Enter</kbd> parse · <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+G</kbd> generate · <kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd> settings |
| **Privacy-first** | Zero backend. Zero uploads. Your data never leaves the browser. |

## Quick Start

### GitHub Pages (no install needed)

1. Enable **GitHub Pages** for your repository (Settings → Pages → Source: `Deploy from a branch`, select `main` + `/docs` or `/root`).
2. Push the contents of the `web/` folder to your repo root (or adjust the GitHub Pages source folder).
3. Visit `https://<your-username>.github.io/<your-repo>/` and you're ready to go.

### Local development

```bash
# Clone and open directly in your browser (double-click index.html)
cd web
open index.html   # or just double-click
```

## How to Use

1. **Upload** your CV via drag-and-drop or the *Choose File* button.
2. **Preview** the extracted text in the preview card.
3. Click **Parse CV** — the app will try your local LLM first, falling back to the built-in parser if no LLM is configured or reachable.
4. **Edit** any field in the form that appears. Add or remove work-experience and education entries as needed.
5. Click **Generate Clean DOCX** to download your polished resume.

## LLM Configuration

By default, the app is configured for a local LLM at:

```
http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions
Model: local-model
```

### Setting up a local LLM

- **Ollama** (recommended): Run `ollama serve` and ensure the OpenAI-compatible API is enabled.
- **LM Studio**: Start the local server (usually `http://localhost:1234/v1/chat/completions`).
- **text-generation-webui / llama.cpp / vLLM**: All expose an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint.

> **CORS note:** The LLM server must allow cross-origin requests from your domain. On `localhost` this is typically already enabled.

To change settings, click the ⚙️ **Settings** button in the header, update the endpoint/model/key/timeout, and click **Test Connection**.

## File Structure

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | Main page — structure, drop zone, preview, form, settings modal |
| `styles.css` | All styling — modern theme, dark mode, animations, responsive |
| `app.js` | Core logic — text extraction, LLM calls, fallback parser, DOCX generation |

### External libraries (loaded via CDN)

| Library | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [PDF.js](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/) | Extract text from PDFs |
| [mammoth.js](https://github.com/mwilliamson/mammoth.js) | Extract text from DOCX |
| [docx](https://github.com/dolanmiu/docx) | Generate DOCX documents |
| [FileSaver.js](https://github.com/eligrey/FileSaver.js) | Trigger file downloads |
| [Tesseract.js](https://github.com/naptha/tesseract.js) | OCR for images (loaded on demand) |

## Keyboard Shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| <kbd>Ctrl + Enter</kbd> | Parse CV |
| <kbd>Ctrl + Shift + G</kbd> | Generate DOCX |
| <kbd>Ctrl + ,</kbd> | Open settings |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Navigate form fields |

## Browser Support

- Chrome / Edge / Firefox / Safari (latest two versions)
- Mobile browsers (responsive layout)
- JavaScript must be enabled.

## License

This is the web edition of the offline CV Builder. See the main project repository for the Python desktop version.

Contains text extraction from PDF/DOCX/images, LLM calls, fallback regex parser, DOCX generation, and data validation. This is the brain of the Python version! |
| **`desktop_app.py`** | **Desktop launcher** — starts the FastAPI server in a background thread on port 5000, waits 2 seconds, then opens your default browser automatically. Keeps running until you hit Ctrl+C. |

## Overview
This file represents a new route for Kaggriculture agent optimization, focusing on hand/hire efficiency, crops, and buy/sell orders while avoiding animal-related strategies.

## Key Changes Made

  - **LATE_GAME**: `["STRAWBERRY", "WHEAT", "MELON"]` (STRAWBERRY prioritized)

### 4. Strategy Stack
- **STRATEGY_STACK**: Changed from `["balanced", "full_animal"]` to `["balanced", "crop_efficiency"]`
- This removes animal-focused strategies and replaces them with crop efficiency

### 5. Overrides Configuration

# ==========================================================================
# CONFIG — edit this block to change behaviour. Nothing below this section
# needs to be touched for day-to-day tuning; every knob here is read live,
# every turn, by the functions further down (see the inline pointers).
# ==========================================================================
CONFIG = {

    # ---- Master hand/action limiter ---------------------------------------
    # Hard ceiling on how many workers (farmer + hired hands) may be given
    # ANY task on a single day, and the value every other "how many hands"
    # calculation in the file is clamped against (crew-size heuristics,
    # quadrant-4 hand cap, etc). If the crew ever grows past this number,
    # the extras simply PASS for the day instead of acting — the day is
    # never crashed or aborted, just gracefully capped.
    "MAX_HANDS_PER_DAY": 12,

    # ---- Seed priorities by game stage -------------------------------------
    # Base seed-buying order for each stage of the game (see GAME_PHASE_DAYS
    # for where each stage starts/ends). Read by _phase_buy_crops(). The
    # first crop in each list is bought first, as long as money/tile
    # headroom allow it.
    "PRIORITY_SEEDS": {
        "EARLY_GAME": ["MELON", "WHEAT", "CARROT"],
        "MID_GAME":   ["MELON", "STRAWBERRY", "WHEAT"],
        "LATE_GAME":  ["STRAWBERRY", "WHEAT", "CARROT"],
    },
    # Day boundaries for the three stages above. EARLY_GAME is day <
    # EARLY_GAME_END; MID_GAME is EARLY_GAME_END <= day < MID_GAME_END;
    # LATE_GAME is everything from MID_GAME_END onward.
    "GAME_PHASE_DAYS": {"EARLY_GAME_END": 6, "MID_GAME_END": 10},

    # ---- Day-0 opening ------------------------------------------------------
    # The purchase plan executed on Day 0, Hour 0. "hires" is how many hands
    # to hire immediately; "orders" is a list of (KIND, ITEM, QTY) tuples
    # with KIND one of "ANIMAL", "SEED", "PRODUCT". Every order is
    # affordability-gated (skipped, not fatal, if money runs short).
    "DAY_ZERO_BUYS": {
        "hires": 5,
        "orders": [
            ("ANIMAL", "SHEEP", 2), ("ANIMAL", "COW", 2),
            ("SEED", "MELON", 4), ("SEED", "WHEAT", 10),
            ("PRODUCT", "WHEAT", 4),
        ],
    },
    # Which day-0 opening actually runs: "CUSTOM" executes DAY_ZERO_BUYS
    # above. Set this to any other key of DAY0_CANDIDATES (e.g. "VERIFIED",
    # "4COW", "4SHEEP", "CROP_FIRST", "MIX_ANIMAL_CROP", ...) to run one of
    # the built-in pre-tuned openings instead, without editing DAY_ZERO_BUYS.
    "DAY0_STRATEGY": "CUSTOM",

    # ---- Per-day overrides ---------------------------------------------------
    # Keyed by day number (0-29). Each entry can set any of:
    #   STOP_WATERING - skip WATER tasks that day
    #   SKIP_HARVEST  - skip HARVEST tasks that day
    #   SKIP_BUYING   - place no market buy orders that day (selling still happens)
    #   PAUSE_ALL     - do nothing at all that day (farmer/hands PASS, no market orders)
    # Example:
    #   "DAILY_OVERRIDES": {
    #       5:  {"STOP_WATERING": True, "SKIP_HARVEST": True},

    #   },
    "DAILY_OVERRIDES": {1: {"STOP_WATERING": True}

    "STRATEGY_STACK": ['balanced', 'full_animal'],

# ==========================================================================
# OVERRIDES — hard, situational rules that punch through every strategy and
# heuristic below. Empty by default (= zero effect, verified baseline).
# Every key is OPTIONAL; leave a section empty ({}) to disable it entirely.
#
# DAY KEYS: every override is keyed by either
#     an int day (e.g. 5)                 -> applies to that day only
#     a (start, end) tuple (e.g. (5, 8))   -> applies to that inclusive range
# You can mix single days and ranges freely within the same override.
#
#   MAX_HIRE_HANDS         {day_or_range: max_total_hands}
#       Hard-caps how many hired hands may be BOUGHT (via HIRE orders) on the
#       given day(s). Existing hands already on payroll are unaffected; this
#       only trims *new* HIRE buy orders once the cap would be exceeded.
#
#   STOP_BUYING             {
#       "ALL":     [day_or_range, ...],                # no purchases at all
#       "LAND":    [day_or_range, ...],                # no BUY_LAND orders
#       "CROPS":   {"MELON": [day_or_range, ...]},      # no MELON seed buys
#       "ANIMALS": {"COW": [day_or_range, ...]},        # no COW buys
#   }
#       Halts buying globally, or of one named crop/animal, for the given
#       window(s). Selling is never affected.
#
#   SPECIFIC_BUYS           {day: [(KIND, ITEM, QTY), ...]}
#       Forces exact purchases on an exact day. KIND is one of "ANIMAL",
#       "SEED", "PRODUCT" (mirrors DAY_ZERO_BUYS). Example:
#           2: [("SEED", "WHEAT", 20)]   # buy 20 wheat seeds on Day 2
#
#   SPECIFIC_SELLS           {day: [(ITEM, QTY), ...]}
#       Forces exact inventory sales on an exact day, added on top of
#       whatever the normal sell logic already decided to sell.
#
#   FORCE_SELL               {day_or_range: [(ITEM, QTY_or_"ALL"), ...]}
#       Same as SPECIFIC_SELLS but supports day ranges and an "ALL" quantity
#       that liquidates every sellable unit of that item on the day it fires.
#
#   PRIORITY_TASKS           {day_or_range: [TASK_TYPE, ...]}
#       Task types (e.g. "HARVEST", "WATER", "FEED", "CARE", "PLANT") listed
#       here get bumped to the top of the task queue for that window.

    ],
}


def _override_day_match(key, day):
    """True if an OVERRIDES day-key (int day, or (start,end) tuple) covers
    `day`."""
    if isinstance(key, (tuple, list)) and len(key) == 2:
        return key[0] <= day <= key[1]
    return key == day


def _override_lookup(section, day):
    """First value in OVERRIDES[section] whose day-key covers `day`, or None.
    Section must be a {day_or_range: value} mapping (not the nested
    STOP_BUYING/dict-of-dicts sections, which have their own helpers)."""
    for key, value in OVERRIDES.get(section, {}).items():
        if _override_day_match(key, day):
            return value
    return None


class OverrideEngine:
    """Applies every OVERRIDES rule to a turn's tasks/buy/sell orders. Each
    method is a pure, additive post-processing pass: called with the normal
    strategy output, it returns a possibly-trimmed/augmented list. When the
    relevant OVERRIDES section is empty, every method is a no-op, so leaving
    OVERRIDES at its defaults reproduces the unmodified agent exactly."""

    # ---- tasks ------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def apply_priority_tasks(tasks, day):
        boost_types = _override_lookup("PRIORITY_TASKS", day)
        if not boost_types:
            return tasks
        for t in tasks:
            if t.get("type") in boost_types:
                t["priority"] = t.get("priority", 0) + 100000
        return tasks

    # ---- buying -------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def apply_stop_buying(orders, day):
        stop_cfg = OVERRIDES.get("STOP_BUYING", {})
        for rng in stop_cfg.get("ALL", []):
            if _override_day_match(rng, day):
                return []
        land_stop = any(_override_day_match(r, day) for r in stop_cfg.get("LAND", []))
        crop_stop = stop_cfg.get("CROPS", {})
        animal_stop = stop_cfg.get("ANIMALS", {})
        out = []
        for o in orders:
            if _is_sequence(o) and o:
                if o[0] == "BUY_LAND" and land_stop:
                    continue
                if len(o) > 1:
                    if o[0] == "BUY_SEED" and any(
                            _override_day_match(r, day) for r in crop_stop.get(o[1], [])):
                        continue
                    if o[0] == "BUY_ANIMAL" and any(
                            _override_day_match(r, day) for r in animal_stop.get(o[1], [])):
                        continue
            out.append(o)
        return out

    @staticmethod
    def apply_force_buy_restriction(orders, day):
        item = _override_lookup("FORCE_BUY_RESTRICTION", day)
        if not item:
            return orders
        return [o for o in orders
                if not (_is_sequence(o) and len(o) > 1 and o[0] in ("BUY_SEED", "BUY_ANIMAL")
                        and o[1] != item)]

    @staticmethod
    def apply_specific_buys(orders, day, money):
        """Force-buy list for this day (day/range keys allowed). Every order is
        affordability-gated against the REAL unit cost and `money` is decremented
        so downstream money estimates never overdraw (FIX)."""
        entries = _override_lookup("SPECIFIC_BUYS", day)
        if not entries or not _override_once("SPECIFIC_BUYS", day):
            return orders, money
        for kind, item, qty in entries:
            if kind == "ANIMAL":
                unit = OverrideEngine._ANIMAL_COST.get(item, 400)
            elif kind == "SEED":
                unit = SEED_COST.get(item, 10)
            elif kind == "PRODUCT":
                unit = BASE_PRICE.get(item, 25)
            else:
                unit = 10
            cost = unit * qty
            if money >= cost:
                orders.append(["BUY_" + kind, item, qty])
                money -= cost
        return orders, money

    @staticmethod
    def apply_max_hire_hands(orders, day, hires_today):
        cap = _override_lookup("MAX_HIRE_HANDS", day)
        if cap is None:
            return orders
        allowed_new = max(0, _int(cap, 0) - hires_today)
        out, hired = [], 0
        for o in orders:
            if _is_sequence(o) and o and o[0] == "HIRE":
                if hired < allowed_new:
                    out.append(o); hired += 1
                # else: drop the excess hire order
            else:
                out.append(o)
        return out

    @staticmethod
    def apply_land_quadrant(orders, day, unlocked_cnt, money):
        target = _override_lookup("BUY_LAND_QUADRANT", day)
        if target is None or unlocked_cnt >= _int(target, 0):
            return orders, money
        if not _override_once("BUY_LAND_QUADRANT:%d" % unlocked_cnt, day):
            return orders, money
        cost = {1: 1000, 2: 2000, 3: 4000}.get(unlocked_cnt)
        if cost is None or money < cost:
            return orders, money
        orders = [o for o in orders if not (_is_sequence(o) and o and o[0] == "BUY_LAND")]
        orders.insert(0, ["BUY_LAND"])
        return orders, money - cost

    # ANIMAL costs, mirrored from the game's own animal prices (see
    # _plan_animals / _last_profitable_buy_day) so this override never has
    # to guess a purchase's real cost.
    _ANIMAL_COST = {ANIMAL_COW: 400, ANIMAL_SHEEP: 500, ANIMAL_GOOSE: 300}

    @staticmethod
    def apply_animal_shop_strategy(orders, day, unlocked_shops, money):
        """Shop-presence -> animal purchase, gated by your own day/range.
        For each shop currently unlocked that appears in the active
        ANIMAL_SHOP_STRATEGY mapping, force-buys the paired animal (skipped
        for the turn, not fatal, if the exact cost isn't affordable)."""
        cfg = _override_lookup("ANIMAL_SHOP_STRATEGY", day)
        if not cfg or not _override_once("ANIMAL_SHOP_STRATEGY", day):
            return orders, money
        shops = set(unlocked_shops or [])
        for shop, spec in cfg.items():
            if shop not in shops:
                continue
            if isinstance(spec, (tuple, list)) and len(spec) == 2:
                animal, qty = spec
            else:
                animal, qty = spec, 1
            qty = max(1, _int(qty, 1))
            unit_cost = OverrideEngine._ANIMAL_COST.get(animal)
            if unit_cost is None:
                continue
            total_cost = unit_cost * qty
            if money >= total_cost:
                orders.append(["BUY_ANIMAL", animal, qty])
                money -= total_cost
        return orders, money

    # ---- selling ------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def apply_specific_sells(orders, day):
        entries = _override_lookup("SPECIFIC_SELLS", day)
        if not entries or not _override_once("SPECIFIC_SELLS", day):
            return orders
        for item, qty in entries:
            orders.append(["SELL", item, qty])
        return orders

    @staticmethod
    def apply_force_sell(orders, day, shed, global_inv, placed_animals,
                         owned_animals=None):
        entries = _override_lookup("FORCE_SELL", day)
        if not entries or not _override_once("FORCE_SELL", day):
            return orders
        herd = owned_animals if owned_animals is not None else placed_animals
        for item, qty in entries:
            if qty == "ALL":
                qty = _sellable_inventory(item, shed, global_inv, day, herd)
            if qty and qty > 0:
                orders.append(["SELL", item, int(qty)])
        return orders


def _shop_driven_species_pick(unlocked_shops):
    """If the currently-unlocked shops form one of the known powerful pairs,
    return the recommended animal species (or list of species) to buy first.
    Otherwise return None.

    Table (see the Full Override Reference): Goose/Eggs pairs, Cow/Milk
    pairs, Sheep/Wool (Yarn Store + anything), Carrot pairs (Pet Cafe).
    Carrot is a crop, not an animal, so that case returns the string
    "CARROT_PRIORITY" instead of a species list (consumed by _plan_seeds).
    If multiple pairs could match, Goose > Cow > Sheep.

    NOTE: pairs are matched as a SUBSET of unlocked_shops (pair <= shops),
    not exact equality — with exact equality these checks go dead the
    moment a third shop unlocks, which is most of the game. If you want the
    stricter "only these two shops, nothing else" behavior, change `<=` to
    `==` below."""
    if not unlocked_shops:
        return None
    shops = set(unlocked_shops)

    # Goose / Eggs pairs
    goose_pairs = [
        {SHOP_BAKERY, SHOP_BRUNCH_SPOT},
        {SHOP_BAKERY, SHOP_FARMERS_MARKET},
        {SHOP_BRUNCH_SPOT, SHOP_FARMERS_MARKET},
        {SHOP_BAKERY, SHOP_PIZZA_SHOP},
        {SHOP_BAKERY, SHOP_ICE_CREAM_SHOP},
    ]
    if any(pair <= shops for pair in goose_pairs):
        return [ANIMAL_GOOSE]

    # Cow / Milk pairs
    cow_pairs = [
        {SHOP_SMOOTHIE_SHOP, SHOP_ICE_CREAM_SHOP},
        {SHOP_PIZZA_SHOP, SHOP_SMOOTHIE_SHOP},
        {SHOP_PIZZA_SHOP, SHOP_ICE_CREAM_SHOP},
        {SHOP_SMOOTHIE_SHOP, SHOP_FARMERS_MARKET},
        {SHOP_SMOOTHIE_SHOP, SHOP_BRUNCH_SPOT},
        {SHOP_ICE_CREAM_SHOP, SHOP_BRUNCH_SPOT},
        {SHOP_PIZZA_SHOP, SHOP_BRUNCH_SPOT},
        {SHOP_PIZZA_SHOP, SHOP_FARMERS_MARKET},
        {SHOP_ICE_CREAM_SHOP, SHOP_FARMERS_MARKET},
    ]
    if any(pair <= shops for pair in cow_pairs):
        return [ANIMAL_COW]

    # Sheep / Wool — Yarn Store is the only Wool drain, pairs with anything.
    if SHOP_YARN_STORE in shops:
        return [ANIMAL_SHEEP]

    # Carrot pairs (Pet Cafe doubles Carrot drain) — crop, not animal.
    if SHOP_PET_CAFE in shops and len(shops) == 2:
        return "CARROT_PRIORITY"

    return None


# ==========================================================================
# OVERSEER — the deterministic decision layer
# ==========================================================================
# The Overseer answers ONE question, at the top of every market decision:
#   "Is there a deterministic rule for the CURRENT state (shops, day,
#   money)?" If yes, it returns a DIRECTIVE dict that the planners MUST
#   follow. If no rule fires, it returns {} and the normal automation
#   (demand rates, phase plan, profit gates, price projections) decides —
#   automation is the FALLBACK, deterministic rules are first.
#
# This is the user's "override first, automation fallback" architecture:
#   - deterministic plans (shop X opened on day 8 -> do Y) live as DATA in
#     OVERRIDES["SHOP_STRATEGY"], not as hard-coded branches scattered
#     through the planners;
#   - the Overseer is the single place that turns those rules into a
#     directive the planners consume;
#   - every planner keeps its own heuristic so the agent degrades gracefully
#     when no rule matches.
#
# Directive keys consumed today (add more here as new triggers are wired):
#   species_order   -> _plan_animals buys in this order (skips demand-rate
#                      reorder AND the hard-coded shop pick helper)
#   carrot_priority -> _plan_seeds puts CARROT first in the buy order
class Overseer:
    """Turns OVERRIDES["SHOP_STRATEGY"] + day/game state into a directive
    the planners must follow. Pure read-only: never mutates state, never
    fails — an empty/malformed rule table degrades to {} (automation)."""

    @staticmethod
    def decide(day, unlocked_shops):
        """First matching OVERRIDES['SHOP_STRATEGY'] rule's directive, or {}.
        Rules are evaluated in list order; the first rule whose shop SET is
        a subset of currently-unlocked shops wins. Optional
        'exact_shop_count' restricts to exactly that many unlocked shops.
        GOOSE directives are dropped when geese are disabled (_geese_on()
        False) — a deterministic rule must never order a species the agent
        cannot even place (A/B: geese regress -10k, so ENABLE_GEESE=False
        means "never buy geese", even if a shop pair says otherwise)."""
        directive = {}
        shops = set(unlocked_shops or [])
        for rule in OVERRIDES.get("SHOP_STRATEGY", []) or []:
            if not isinstance(rule, dict):
                continue
            need = set(rule.get("shops") or [])
            if not need or not need <= shops:
                continue
            exact = rule.get("exact_shop_count")
            if exact is not None and len(shops) != _int(exact, -1):
                continue
            directive = dict(rule.get("then") or {})
            break
        # Hard goose gate at the SOURCE: geese-off rules never emit GOOSE.
        # If stripping leaves an empty species_order the directive collapses
        # to {} — no override fired, automation decides (cleanest fallback).
        if not _geese_on() and isinstance(directive.get("species_order"), list):
            directive["species_order"] = [
                s for s in directive["species_order"] if s != ANIMAL_GOOSE]
            if not directive["species_order"]:
                directive.pop("species_order")
        return directive

def _override_once(name, day):
    """True the FIRST time this (override name, day) pair is seen this game;
    False on every later call for the same day. agent() runs once per HOUR,
    not once per day, so any override that INJECTS an order (as opposed to
    just filtering the existing list) must be gated by this or it fires
    again on every hourly call — e.g. buying another cow every single hour
    of the day instead of once. Filters (stop-buying, restriction, hire cap)
    don't need this; only the injectors do."""
    global _OVERRIDE_FIRED
    if _OVERRIDE_FIRED is None:
        _OVERRIDE_FIRED = {}
    seen_today = _OVERRIDE_FIRED.setdefault(day, set())
    if name in seen_today:
        return False
    seen_today.add(name)
    return True

        "max_animals": MAX_ANIMALS,
        "early_animal_rush": EARLY_ANIMAL_RUSH,

        "hand_bias": 1,
    },
}

class StrategyManager:
    """Wraps STRATEGY_DEFINITIONS + CONFIG['STRATEGY_STACK'] so strategies can
    be toggled on/off or reordered without touching any other part of the
    file. enable()/disable()/set_stack() mutate CONFIG['STRATEGY_STACK'] in
    place, so every existing call site (which reads CONFIG live via
    _strategy_effects()) picks up the change on the very next call."""

    def __init__(self, definitions, config):
        self.definitions = definitions
        self.config = config

    def available(self):
        """Names of every strategy that could be added to the stack."""
        return list(self.definitions.keys())

    def active_stack(self):
        """Currently-enabled strategy names, in apply order."""
        return list(self.config.get("STRATEGY_STACK") or [])

    def enable(self, name):
        """Turn a strategy ON (append to the stack) if it isn't already."""
        if name in self.definitions and name not in self.active_stack():
            self.config.setdefault("STRATEGY_STACK", []).append(name)

    def disable(self, name):
        """Turn a strategy OFF (remove from the stack) if present."""
        stack = self.config.get("STRATEGY_STACK")
        if stack and name in stack:
            stack.remove(name)

    def set_stack(self, names):
        """Replace the whole stack at once, in the given order."""
        self.config["STRATEGY_STACK"] = [n for n in names if n in self.definitions]

    def effects(self):
        """Fold the active stack into one effective-settings dict.
        Strategies are applied in list order: for any plain (scalar) setting
        the LAST strategy in the stack wins; 'seed_priority_boost' lists are
        combined across the whole stack instead of overwritten, so stacking
        strategies layers their crop preferences rather than discarding
        earlier ones."""
        effects = dict(self.definitions.get("balanced", {}))
        effects["seed_priority_boost"] = []
        for name in self.active_stack():
            cfg = self.definitions.get(name)
            if not cfg:
                continue
            for key, value in cfg.items():
                if key == "seed_priority_boost":
                    for crop in value:
                        if crop not in effects["seed_priority_boost"]:
                            effects["seed_priority_boost"].append(crop)
                else:
                    effects[key] = value
        return effects


STRATEGIES = StrategyManager(STRATEGY_DEFINITIONS, CONFIG)


def _strategy_effects():
    """Back-compat shim — every existing call site uses this name."""
    return STRATEGIES.effects()

def _daily_overrides(day):
    """DAILY_OVERRIDES entry for this day (int day OR (start,end) range keys),
    merged LIFO across matching ranges, or {} if none is configured."""
    table = CONFIG.get("DAILY_OVERRIDES", {}) or {}
    out = {}
    for key, value in table.items():
        if _override_day_match(key, day) and isinstance(value, dict):
            out.update(value)
    return out

def _game_phase(day):
    """Which PRIORITY_SEEDS bucket `day` falls into, per GAME_PHASE_DAYS."""
    bounds = CONFIG.get("GAME_PHASE_DAYS", {})
    if day < bounds.get("EARLY_GAME_END", 6):
        return "EARLY_GAME"
    if day < bounds.get("MID_GAME_END", 12):
        return "MID_GAME"
    return "LATE_GAME"


# [SCANNER] _detect_game_phase: Economic-state game-phase detector (Gap 4).
def _detect_game_phase(day, money=0.0, active_crops=None):
    """Dynamic PRIORITY_SEEDS phase: _game_phase's cutover is a fixed day,
    but a strong cash/strawberry position can justify pivoting earlier (e.g.
    a big day-10 melon harvest funding the strawberry ramp before day 12).
    Gated by DYNAMIC_GAME_PHASE; when OFF this returns exactly _game_phase's
    verdict. When ON, the dynamic verdict can only PULL the phase EARLIER,
    never later — the fixed-day rule stays the floor, so a slow start never
    regresses below the tuned fixed-day baseline."""
    fixed = _game_phase(day)
    if not DYNAMIC_GAME_PHASE:
        return fixed
    active_crops = active_crops or {}
    order = ["EARLY_GAME", "MID_GAME", "LATE_GAME"]
    if money >= DYNAMIC_PHASE_MONEY.get("LATE_GAME", 4000) or \
       active_crops.get("STRAWBERRY", 0) >= DYNAMIC_PHASE_STRAWBERRY:
        dynamic = "LATE_GAME"
    elif money >= DYNAMIC_PHASE_MONEY.get("MID_GAME", 1500):
        dynamic = "MID_GAME"
    else:
        dynamic = "EARLY_GAME"
    return dynamic if order.index(dynamic) > order.index(fixed) else fixed

def _max_hands_per_day():
    return max(1, _int(CONFIG.get("MAX_HANDS_PER_DAY", HANDS_CAP), HANDS_CAP))

def _pass():
    return {"farmer": ["PASS"], "hands": [], "market": []}

def _geese_on():
    """Runtime goose switch. When GEESE_DEMAND_ENABLE is ON, geese activate
    only if an egg-demanding shop (Bakery/Brunch Spot) unlocked early; else
    they stay OFF (the verified -10k regression). A/B 2026-08-09: geese
    regress even when Bakery+Brunch are unlocked (egg income ~$5-6k can't
    offset the coop tiles + worker time), so this knob defaults OFF."""
    return _GEESE_ACTIVE

def _safe_get(d, key, default):
    if isinstance(d, dict):
        return d.get(key, default)
    return default

def _int(value, default=0):
    try:
        if value is None:
            return default
        return int(value)
    except Exception:
        return default

def _float(value, default=0.0):
    try:
        if value is None:
            return default
        return float(value)
    except Exception:
        return default

def _is_sequence(obj):
    return isinstance(obj, (list, tuple))

def _in_bounds(tiles, x, y):
    try:
        return 0 <= y < len(tiles) and 0 <= x < len(tiles[y])
    except Exception:
        return False

def _step_towards(fx, fy, tx, ty):
    if tx < fx: return ["WEST"]
    if tx > fx: return ["EAST"]
    if ty < fy: return ["NORTH"]
    if ty > fy: return ["SOUTH"]
    return ["PASS"]

def _safe_step_towards(fx, fy, tx, ty, tiles):
    """Return the first walkable step toward (tx,ty), else PASS."""
    preferred = _step_towards(fx, fy, tx, ty)
    if preferred == ["PASS"]:
        return ["PASS"]
    # Check preferred direction
    dx, dy = 0, 0
    if preferred[0] == "WEST":  dx = -1
    elif preferred[0] == "EAST": dx = 1
    elif preferred[0] == "NORTH": dy = -1
    elif preferred[0] == "SOUTH": dy = 1
    if _in_bounds(tiles, fx+dx, fy+dy) and tiles[fy+dy][fx+dx] != "LOCKED":
        return preferred
    # If blocked, try all other directions in any order
    for dir in (["WEST"], ["EAST"], ["NORTH"], ["SOUTH"]):
        if dir == preferred:
            continue
        dx, dy = 0, 0
        if dir[0] == "WEST":  dx = -1
        elif dir[0] == "EAST": dx = 1
        elif dir[0] == "NORTH": dy = -1
        elif dir[0] == "SOUTH": dy = 1
        if _in_bounds(tiles, fx+dx, fy+dy) and tiles[fy+dy][fx+dx] != "LOCKED":
            return dir
    return ["PASS"]

def _manhattan(a, b):
    return abs(a[0] - b[0]) + abs(a[1] - b[1])

def _fib_cost(n):
    a, b = 1, 1
    for _ in range(max(0, n)):
        a, b = b, a + b
    return a

def _quadrant(x, y, tiles):
    half = max(1, len(tiles) // 2)
    if x < half and y < half: return QUAD_NW
    if x >= half and y < half: return QUAD_NE
    if x < half and y >= half: return QUAD_SW
    return QUAD_SE

def _is_plant(tile):
    return isinstance(tile, dict) and _safe_get(tile, "kind", "") == "PLANT"

def _is_weed(tile):
    return isinstance(tile, dict) and _safe_get(tile, "kind", "") == "WEED"

def _plant_ready(tile, day):
    crop = _safe_get(tile, "crop", "WHEAT")
    yu = _int(_safe_get(tile, "yield_units", 0), 0)
    pd = _int(_safe_get(tile, "planted_day", 0), 0)
    age = max(0, day - pd)
    if crop in ONGOING_CROPS:
        return yu > 0
    md = CROP_MAX_DAY.get(crop, 4)
    my = CROP_MAX_YIELD.get(crop, 4)
    # The GAME's HARVEST no-ops if age < first_yield_day (melons accumulate
    # yield 6 by day 8 but only mature day 10 — see _game_src line 397).
    # Requiring maturity here stops workers from walking to immature melons
    # every hour (wasted ~20 actions/day, the empty-tile gap days 8-9).
    first_yield = CROP_FIRST_YIELD.get(crop, md)
    return yu > 0 and age >= first_yield and (age >= md or yu >= my)

# [SCANNER] _scan_active_crops: Counts active (planted, non-weed) crops per type across all tiles.
def _scan_active_crops(tiles):
    active = {}
    if not _is_sequence(tiles): return active
    for row in tiles:
        if not _is_sequence(row): continue
        for tile in row:
            if _is_plant(tile):
                c = _safe_get(tile, "crop", "WHEAT")
                active[c] = active.get(c, 0) + 1
    return active

def _count_placed_animals(tiles):
    return sum(1 for row in tiles if _is_sequence(row)
               for t in row if isinstance(t, dict)
               and t.get("kind") in ("PASTURE", "COOP") and t.get("animal"))

def _count_owned_animals(tiles, shed=None, inventories=None):
    """Total herd = placed animals + animals still sitting in the shed
    (bought but not yet placed) + animals currently CARRIED by workers
    (picked up from the shed, not yet placed on a pasture). All three
    groups need pasture space, feed and care, so hiring/feeding should
    look at the whole herd, not just the tiles already stocked.
    `inventories` is the private unit-inventory list; carried animals
    appear there as COW/SHEEP/GOOSE (verified in-game: workers carry
    animals for a few turns between shed pickup and pasture placement)."""
    placed = _count_placed_animals(tiles)
    total = placed
    if isinstance(shed, dict):
        total += (_int(_safe_get(shed, ANIMAL_COW, 0), 0)
                  + _int(_safe_get(shed, ANIMAL_SHEEP, 0), 0)
                  + (_int(_safe_get(shed, ANIMAL_GOOSE, 0), 0) if _geese_on() else 0))
    if _is_sequence(inventories):
        for inv in inventories:
            if not isinstance(inv, dict):
                continue
            total += (_int(_safe_get(inv, ANIMAL_COW, 0), 0)
                      + _int(_safe_get(inv, ANIMAL_SHEEP, 0), 0)
                      + (_int(_safe_get(inv, ANIMAL_GOOSE, 0), 0) if _geese_on() else 0))
    return total

def _count_empty_pastures(tiles):
    return sum(1 for row in tiles if _is_sequence(row)
               for t in row if isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("kind") == "PASTURE" and not t.get("animal"))

def _count_pastures(tiles):
    return sum(1 for row in tiles if _is_sequence(row)
               for t in row if isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("kind") == "PASTURE")

def _count_coops(tiles):
    return sum(1 for row in tiles if _is_sequence(row)
               for t in row if isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("kind") == "COOP")

def _count_placed_geese(tiles):
    return sum(1 for row in tiles if _is_sequence(row)
               for t in row if isinstance(t, dict)
               and t.get("kind") == "COOP" and t.get("animal") == ANIMAL_GOOSE)

def _count_placed_species(tiles, animal):
    """Placed animals of one species (COW/SHEEP/GOOSE) on tiles."""
    return sum(1 for row in tiles if _is_sequence(row)
               for t in row if isinstance(t, dict)
               and t.get("kind") in ("PASTURE", "COOP") and t.get("animal") == animal)

def _desired_hands(day, money, active_crops, placed_animals, forecast_free=None,
                   unlocked_cnt=3, owned_animals=None):
    if day >= LIQUIDATION_DAY: return 2
    total = sum(active_crops.values()) if isinstance(active_crops, dict) else 0
    herd = owned_animals if owned_animals is not None else placed_animals
    if day <= 1: base = 5
    elif day <= 5: base = 3 + total // 6 + herd // 4
    elif day <= 10: base = 5 + total // 5 + herd // 3
    else: base = 7 + total // 5 + herd // 2
    base += _strategy_effects()["hand_bias"]
    if FORECAST_DRIVES_HANDS and isinstance(forecast_free, dict):
        # Tiles freeing within the horizon become replant work (PLANT + a few
        # days of WATER). The base heuristic only counts *currently planted*
        # tiles, so add hands for the upcoming load. Divisor = freed tiles per
        # extra hand; larger = more conservative.
        upcoming = sum(forecast_free.values())
        if upcoming > 0:
            base += max(1, (upcoming + FORECAST_HANDS_DIVISOR - 1) // FORECAST_HANDS_DIVISOR)
    floor = 3 if day <= 5 else 2
    # 4th quadrant opens 25 more plantable tiles -> allow a bigger crew so the
    # new land is actually watered (user: "open more hired hands if needed").
    cap = QUADRANT_4_HANDS_CAP if (QUADRANT_4_UNLOCK and unlocked_cnt >= 4) else HANDS_CAP
    cap = min(cap, _max_hands_per_day())
    want = max(floor, min(cap, base))
    # HANDS_EXACT / HANDS_MIN / HANDS_MAX overrides (day or range keys).
    exact = _override_lookup("HANDS_EXACT", day)
    if exact is not None:
        want = _int(exact, want)
    low = _override_lookup("HANDS_MIN", day)
    if low is not None:
        want = max(want, _int(low, want))
    high = _override_lookup("HANDS_MAX", day)
    if high is not None:
        want = min(want, _int(high, want))
    return want

# ==========================================================================
# TURN-AWARE BUDGET PLANNER
# ==========================================================================
# One place that decides ALL market spending for the current turn, so the
# agent plans as a whole instead of buying pieces ad hoc. Every decision is
# turn-aware: value decays with remaining time because
#   - a hand hired at hour 20 only works ~4 hours but costs the same
#     Fibonacci wage as one hired at hour 0;
#   - an animal bought with < first_yield_days left never pays back its cost;
#   - seeds bought after MIN_PLANT_DAYS can never be harvested;
#   - land bought with too few days left never hosts a harvestable crop.

def _turns_info(day, hour):
    """(hours_left_today, days_left_total) — the planning horizon."""
    hours_today = max(0, 24 - hour)
    days_left = max(0, 30 - day)
    return hours_today, days_left


# [SCANNER] _forecast_free_tiles: Projects which tiles free up (harvest-ready) within a horizon of days.
def _forecast_free_tiles(tiles, day, horizon=FORECAST_HORIZON_DAYS):
    """Day tracker: count, per crop, how many plants will be harvestable
    (tile frees up for replanting) within `horizon` days from today.
    One-time crops (wheat/carrot/melon) free when their age reaches
    CROP_MAX_DAY; ongoing crops (strawberry) free only after they have
    banked max yield and decay to a weed (then get dug)."""
    free = {}
    if not _is_sequence(tiles): return free
    for row in tiles:
        if not _is_sequence(row): continue
        for tile in row:
